summary: Client-facing timeouts for extremely long prompts combined with very large max_tokens during extended-output generation
description:
Issue summary:
Customers are observing client-side timeouts (HTTP 504 or streaming disconnect) when requests include a very large prompt (long conversation history + documents) and a large max_tokens target for generation (~50k+ output tokens). The problem manifests intermittently but is reproducible with the same inputs and appears correlated with the combined token footprint (prompt tokens + max_tokens) that causes prolonged per-request serving time or backend stalls.

Impact:
- DocuMind (dedicated) reports 60% of extended-generation requests failing with timeouts in nightly batch runs, blocking their indexing pipeline.
- Users see streaming disconnects and truncated outputs; retries frequently hit rate-limits or resource contention.
- Business impact: critical data ingestion delayed; customer requests escalation to enterprise success.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated cluster: prod-us-west dedicated pool for DocuMind
- Model variants: redwood-open-7b-v2 (fp16) and redwood-compat-13b-quant (int8)
- Client uses streaming API with chunked transfer, max_tokens configured per request at 50k in repro cases

Steps to reproduce:
1) Assemble long prompt: ~80k tokens combined from multi-document context + conversation history
2) Call /v1/generate (streaming) with max_tokens set to 50,000 and stop sequences disabled
3) Observe streaming connection: partial tokens arrive for ~30-90s then stream terminates with client-side 504 or connection reset
4) Repeat with same payload; behavior reproduces ~7/10 attempts on dedicated pool during moderate load

Observed behavior:
- Streaming stops mid-generation; server returns no explicit 5xx in some cases.
- When server 5xx is returned, it is often 502/504 from api-gateway.
- On serving nodes, we see long-running inference workers holding KV cache entries and high GPU memory pressure in some repros.

Expected behavior:
- Long-running generations should either stream until completion within configured system SLOs or gracefully return a clear 5xx with retryable flag.

Attachments/Logs:
- Customer-provided request id: req_3f9a7c2e-docu-03
- Sample payload (redacted) attached in ticket attachments
- Partial server logs: API gateway trace: https://logs.redwood.ai/gw/trace/req_3f9a7c2e-docu-03 (redacted link)
- Serving runtime logs: node-12 inference worker stack traces (included in attachments)

2026-03-11 09:37 - Runtime Eng (Priya Rao): Found a path where extremely long max_tokens keeps the request in a hot execution slot preventing KV cache eviction; scheduler's preemption threshold not triggering due to inaccurate duration estimate. Raising hypothesis in investigation notes.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Scheduler duration estimator underpredicts for extremely long-generation requests because it extrapolates from prefix distribution. This leads to long-lived GPU slots and upstream gateway timeouts.

Hypothesis 2: KV cache eviction is deferred for active sessions; with large max_tokens the session holds cache and prevents necessary eviction causing memory pressure and intermittent OOMs on serving nodes.

Observed: node-12 inference worker had sustained GPU memory utilization >95% during repro; multiple long-tail allocations in per-request profiler. See internal dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/longgen/serving-overview?var=node=node-12
Repro steps executed in staging with dedicated pool simulation; confirmed streaming disconnects when combined token footprint >120k tokens and max_tokens >40k under moderate cluster load
Temporary mitigation validated: client windowing reduces peak GPU residency and avoids gateway 504s. However this increases request count and may affect throughput/cost for customer.
Related prior tickets: SUP-72109 highlights related timeouts after KV eviction; this issue differs in that it is triggered by combined prompt + max_tokens rather than eviction timing alone.
resolution:
Workaround: Advised customer to split generation into smaller windowed calls (<=8k max_tokens) and enable client-side streaming reconnect with resume tokens.

Short-term fix (rolled to prod-uc1 on 2026-03-12): Adjust scheduler to set conservative max-execution-time cap for single-request generations (default cap 120s) and improve duration estimator for requests with extremely large max_tokens. Also added a preemption path to allow eviction of lower-priority jobs when a request exceeds the conservative cap.

Long-term actions:
- Implement improved KV cache eviction policy that accounts for active session age and expected remaining tokens.
- Add server-side streaming heartbeat to avoid silent disconnects and return clearer 5xx with retryable flags when preemption occurs.
- Update documentation and SDK examples with recommended patterns for very long outputs (windowing, resumable tokens).

Customer impact and follow-up: DocuMind confirmed nightly job succeeds with workaround. Billing impact: increased number of requests due to windowing may increase tokens/requests; finance to follow up with customer success on adjustments.

Linked PRs and runbooks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1834, https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Long+Context+Timeout+Runbook
